title: Equivariant semistable modification of a marked nodal tower
statement: A trait means the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. A complete strictly henselian trait has a maximal-ideal-adically complete henselian coordinate ring with separably closed residue field. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic. Let $T$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait and $Y_d\to\cdots\to Y_0=T$ a marked split nodal tower of length $d\ge1$. Let a finite group $G$ act equivariantly on this tower (including possibly nontrivially on $T$) with the splitting property on fibre dual graphs described below. Then there exist an integral regular scheme $Z$, projective over $T$, and a $G$-equivariant projective birational morphism $h:Z\to Y_d$. Here birational means that $h$ restricts to an isomorphism over a dense open of $Y_d$. The map $Z\to T$ is strictly semistable: etale locally $Z$ has an etale $T$-morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(t_1\cdots t_r-\pi)$ with $1\le r\le n$, where $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\pi$ is a uniformizer. The reduced inverse image of $B_d$ is a strict normal crossings divisor (etale locally the zero locus of a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters). A marked split nodal tower over a trait $T$ is a tower $Y_d\xrightarrow{f_d}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_1}Y_0=T$ of integral schemes, each $f_i$ projective and flat of finite presentation with geometrically connected reduced fibres of pure dimension one whose only singularities are ordinary double points (completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$). Write $B_0=T_s$ for the closed point. Each $f_i$ has finitely many disjoint sections $\sigma_{ij}$ in its relative smooth locus; set $B_i=f_i^{-1}(B_{i-1})\cup\bigcup_j\sigma_{ij}(Y_{i-1})$ as a closed set. The map $f_i$ is smooth outside $B_{i-1}$. Split means that each fibre's irreducible components are geometrically irreducible and each of its nodes and its two branches are rational over the residue field of the base point. For a group action, the tower is equivariant, the unions of sections are stable, and the stabilizer of a base point acts trivially on the dual graph of its fibre. The dual graph has one vertex for each geometric irreducible component, one edge with its two ends for each node, and an attached marked leg for each section. Integral, regular, flat, finite type, finite, projective, and etale use [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the base. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and geometric integrality, reducedness, connectedness and irreducibility as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].
